selection_rationale: Selected by a model-output-blind, memory-bounded joint search over 216 max-QRS, R-rise, and ST-delay combinations, followed by a 28-point sample-grid refinement and all-exam validation. Relative to pathology_qrs220 on all 106340 CODE-Test lead-beat units, max_qrs_interval=204 ms and typical_st_segment=164 ms increased complete Prominence delineations from 94458 (88.83%) to 94759 (89.11%) and DWT/Prominence common support from 76692 (72.12%) to 77064 (72.47%). Positive-cohort common support increased for 1dAVb from 2133 to 2144 units, RBBB from 2847 to 2866, and LBBB from 1819 to 1834. A descriptive post-selection 2000-resample exam-cluster bootstrap estimated the common-support gain as +0.350 percentage points (95% interval +0.196 to +0.502); it is not an independent selection-adjusted confidence interval. The morphology-positive suspicious-duration unit rate changed from 9.72% to 10.05%, remaining within the predeclared +0.5 percentage-point admissibility bound. PR and T medians were unchanged; QRS median changed from 100.0 to 103.3 ms because the complete-unit population changed, while the final 246.7 ms maximum QRS duration was preserved. Final R/T basepoint windows remain 250/200 ms, so coverage was not gained by truncating returned region boundaries. In LBBB exam 522, Prominence completeness remained 87/156, common support remained 53/156, and the displayed beat remained Prominence-complete in 9/12 leads and DWT/Prominence-common in 7/12 leads. No checkpoint, prediction, probability, attribution, or Shapley output was consulted; clinical fiducial ground truth remains unavailable.
